absent: Numeric values of scheduling constants such as zero nice load, capacity scale, infinite runtime, clamp counts and deltas, bucket counts, maximum real time priority, tick length, and fixed point shift are not shown.
Full type definitions for task group, runqueue, fair and real time queues and entities, bandwidth controls, averaging state, clamp entries, and clock data are not shown.
Allocation cache behavior, node topology, per CPU pointer mechanics, and global runqueue array layout are not shown.
Attachment and throttle synchronization performed during fair online activation beyond invocation are not shown.
Timer callback behavior for fair period and slack and real time period enforcement is not shown.
Extended scheduler weight default, bandwidth enforcement, and runqueue clock hook effects are not shown.
Autogroup management beyond an empty release hook is not shown.
Runqueue lock acquisition, flag definitions for clock updates, and feature flag control are not shown.
Interrupt time, paravirt steal time, frequency and capacity scaling, delay accounting, and tracing effects on load averages are not shown.

findings.text: Scheduler group creation allocates a zeroed group object, initializes fair and real time subgroup state plus extended scheduler and utilization clamp state, and returns the new group or a no memory error marker on failure with prior partial state released.

Fair group management provides allocation that establishes per CPU queue storage, default share value and bandwidth inheritance, and release that frees the per CPU storage; a configuration without group support reduces both to trivial success or no operation.

Real time group management provides allocation that reserves per CPU queue and entity arrays and initializes bandwidth and per CPU entries when group scheduling is enabled, and release that frees those arrays; when disabled both reduce to immediate success or no operation.

Group online publication and fair online attachment expose interfaces that link a new group into global and parental collections and then attach its per CPU fair entities under runqueue protection with clock refresh and throttle synchronization.

Runqueue clock refresh, per CPU scheduler clock queries, and load average updates expose interfaces for advancing runqueue time, obtaining monotonic CPU time from stable or per CPU sources, and folding elapsed time and interrupt time into exponential averages.

Queue and bandwidth initialization helpers expose interfaces that prepare empty fair and real time runqueues, bind entities into parental hierarchies with depth and weight defaults, and establish infinite quota and timer state for enforcement.

Extended scheduler group initialization exposes an interface that assigns default weight, default bandwidth period, infinite quota and non idle marking; an alternate configuration provides an empty variant.
Entity average initialization exposes an interface that clears averaging state and seeds task load from scaled weight while leaving group load at zero.
If fair or real time subgroup reservation fails, creation releases any partial group storage and reports no memory rather than returning a half initialized group.

Successful fair reservation guarantees usable queue storage for every possible CPU, default shares, inherited bandwidth limits, and per CPU entity linkage with runnable averaging seeded; any missing queue aborts with failure.

When real time group scheduling is active, successful reservation guarantees per CPU queue and entity objects, bandwidth period derived from global setting with zero runtime, per queue runtime copied from bandwidth, and parental entity linkage; otherwise success requires no storage.

Root group is identified by address comparison and has no scheduling entity; non root fair entities attach either to the local base queue at depth zero when parentless or to the parental queue with incremented depth, always carry guaranteed weight, and record owning queue and runqueue.

Real time per CPU entries record owning group and runqueue in indexed arrays, bind child entities to either the local base queue or the parental queue, initialize run linkage, and tolerate absent child pointers.
New group utilization clamp requests start at neutral extremes without user marking while effective clamp values inherit the parental effective values for every clamp identifier.
Clamp values map to bucket indices by scaled division capped at the final bucket, and stored entries always carry value plus derived bucket plus user flag.

Fresh fair bandwidth state carries zero runtime, infinite quota and hierarchical quota inheritance, default period, zero burst, empty throttled collection and unstarted slack; fresh real time bandwidth carries configured period with zero runtime.
Averaging state starts cleared; task entities seed load average from scaled weight while group entities remain at zero to reflect absence of attached load.

Runqueue time never moves backward; negative deltas are discarded, skip flagged updates bypass entirely, double updates are flagged when the corresponding feature is active, and task time only advances after interrupt and steal portions are removed with clamping.

Local and remote scheduler clocks are coupled by retaining the larger of the two values so the pair moves monotonically; local reads clamp between a lower bound covering prior time and global offset and an upper bound covering one tick ahead.

Load summation ignores backward time, quantizes elapsed time in approximately microsecond units, decays historic sums on period boundaries of about one millisecond, and forces runnable and running contributions to zero whenever load weight is zero.
Release paths tolerate disabled modes and absent arrays, freeing only present per CPU objects and arrays plus fair per CPU storage and autogroup state.
Global group publication serializes list and parental linkage under an interrupt saving spin lock covering tail insertion, parental assignment, children head setup and sibling linkage.
Fair online attachment acquires each runqueue lock in turn with interrupt protection while refreshing that runqueue clock and attaching the corresponding entity and throttle state before release.
Runqueue clock refresh requires the target runqueue lock to be held by the caller, as asserted on entry.
Bandwidth, removal and runtime protection initializes dedicated raw spin locks for fair bandwidth, fair removal, real time queue runtime and real time bandwidth during object setup.
Scheduler clock coupling uses lock free 64 bit compare exchange with retry loops rather than blocking locks, including a narrow word safe path that re reads local time to avoid torn observations.

Task group state as observed aggregates fair queue storage under cfs_rq with share count under shares and limits under cfs_bandwidth, real time storage under rt_rq and rt_se with limits under rt_bandwidth, extended parameters under scx covering weight and bandwidth period and quota with idle marking, clamp vectors under uclamp_req and uclamp, and linkage under list with parent plus children and siblings.

Fair runqueue state as observed carries ordered tasks under tasks_timeline with initial offset under zero_vruntime and protection under removed plus owner under tg and runqueue under rq with enable flag under runtime_enabled and collections under throttled_list with companion lists; per CPU state pairs one queue with one entity linking cfs_rq and my_q with parent and depth plus load weight.

Real time runqueue state as observed carries a priority array under active with bitmap plus current and next priority under highest_prio and flags under overloaded and queued with boosted count under rt_nr_boosted and pushable collection plus timing under rt_time with throttle flag under rt_throttled and runtime under rt_runtime with lock and owner under tg and runqueue under rq; bandwidth carries period under rt_period with runtime under rt_runtime and lock with timer; entities link rt_rq and my_q with parent and run_list.

Fair bandwidth control as observed aggregates protection under lock with runtime under runtime and quota under quota plus period under period and burst under burst with inheritance under hierarchical_quota and throttled collection plus period timer with slack timer and started flag under slack_started.

Averaging state as observed aggregates sums under load_sum and runnable_sum and util_sum with average under load_avg plus period share under period_contrib and stamp under last_update_time; clamp entries carry value with bucket under bucket_id and flag under user_defined; load weight carries weight with cached inverse under inv_weight.

Runqueue timing state as observed aggregates main clock under clock with task clock under clock_task and flags under clock_update_flags plus previous interrupt stamp under prev_irq_time and steal stamp under prev_steal_time_rq with current task under curr and interrupt average under avg_irq; per CPU scheduler clock state aggregates current clock with tick snapshots under tick_raw and tick_gtod plus global offsets.

Group objects progress from zeroed allocation through fair reservation then real time reservation then extended and clamp setup to published linkage and per CPU attachment; any reservation failure diverts to release of fair and real time and autogroup state with error return.

Fair bandwidth enforcement starts with period timer configured for absolute pinned monotonic expiry at a randomized offset within one period and slack timer configured for relative monotonic expiry but marked not started.

Runqueue clock update acts as a small flag machine where skip bypasses work, otherwise an updated mark is set and double marking triggers a one time warning when enabled before time is sampled and accumulated.

Per CPU clock queries select among stable direct time with offset, early non running fallback, remote coupling for foreign CPUs and local clamping for the current CPU, all under different build configurations.

Load accounting progresses from elapsed quantization through historic decay on period crossing to segment contribution calculation and sum accumulation, signalling callers when a period boundary was crossed so averages and tracing can refresh.
Real time throttling starts dequeued with zero queued time and unthrottled marking, runtime disabled until bandwidth values are copied during group reservation.

Group creation and publication form the external entry surface for new scheduling groups, with creation returning either a usable group or an error marker and publication making it globally visible after parental linkage.

Runqueue clock refresh and per CPU clock reads form the timing entry surface, with the former advancing runqueue and task clocks under lock and the latter supplying CPU time for that advance plus weak fallback based on tick counts.
Fair online attachment forms the per CPU activation entry that must run after publication to bind each CPU entity and synchronize throttling under runqueue protection.

Partial allocation without unwinding would leak per CPU fair storage or real time arrays; the observed paths release prior state on any failure and free paired queue objects when companion entity reservation fails.
Synchronized period timers across groups would cause thundering expiry; the observed setup staggers initial expiry with a random offset bounded by one period.
Torn narrow word clock reads and concurrent coupling updates could corrupt monotonicity; the observed code retries atomic update until success and re samples local time on the narrow path.

Interrupt and steal time observed inside a skipped interval could drive task time backward; the observed accounting clamps each portion to the elapsed delta and carries remainder via updated previous stamps.
Backward time during clock source transitions could corrupt exponential sums; the observed summation detects negative deltas, resynchronizes the last update stamp and skips accumulation.

Publishing a group without a parent or attaching entities without holding runqueue locks would corrupt global lists and fair trees; the observed online path warns on missing parent and holds each runqueue lock during attach with asserted protection for clock updates.
The default bandwidth period used for fair and extended scheduler group setup equals 100000 microseconds.
The fair share and group entity weight default is the zero nice load constant with inverse cache cleared to zero.
Neutral clamp extremes are zero for minimum and full capacity scale for maximum.
Initial fair queue virtual time offset equals negated one shifted left by twenty.
Fresh real time queues initialize highest priority tracking to one below maximum priority with a sentinel bit set at maximum priority and all lower bits cleared.
Load summation quantizes time by ten binary places corresponding to about one microsecond and defines a period as 1024 such units corresponding to about one millisecond.
Fresh fair bandwidth quota, hierarchical quota fallback and extended scheduler quota use the infinite runtime marker with zero runtime and burst.
Weak scheduler clock fallback derives nanoseconds from tick delta scaled by seconds to nanoseconds divided by tick rate.
Global real time period derives from scheduler control period scaled by nanoseconds per microsecond.
Load downscaling either preserves weight identically or shifts right by the scheduler fixed point amount with a minimum result of two for non zero inputs.
